media.altText: Detail of a 1955 magazine photograph showing Franz Waxman in glasses, playing a saxophone.
media.description: The printed caption identifies the two men by what they are holding rather than by position: “FRANZ WAXMAN (with saxophone), music director and conductor of the 1955 Los Angeles Music Festival, rehearses with Les Brown for the opening night concert of the Festival on June 6. Waxman conducted Brown's Band of Renown and the Festival Symphony Orchestra in the West Coast premiere of Liebermann's Concerto for Jazz Band and Symphony Orchestra.” The reproduced detail shows the man holding the saxophone. The photograph is credited “Photo: Dave Pell.”
media.publicCaption: Franz Waxman, documented in connection with Trouble for Two (1936), A Day at the Races (1937) and The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn (1939), rehearses with Les Brown's Band of Renown for the opening concert of the Los Angeles Music Festival in June 1955, which Waxman conducted.
media.publicCreditLine: Photograph credited to Dave Pell; Musical Courier, vol. 152, no. 1 (July 1955), p. 27; Summy-Birchard Publishing Company; scanned copy at the Internet Archive.
media.rightsNote: Public domain in the United States. The photograph was published in Musical Courier in July 1955, when copyright required renewal after twenty-eight years. The Online Books Page inventory compiled from the Catalog of Copyright Entries and Copyright Office records lists May 1961 as the first renewed issue of the title, indicating that the 1955 issue copyright was not renewed and expired on 1 January 1984. The inventory notes that some individual contributions were renewed separately; no separate registration has been identified for this photograph, which carries only a caption credit. The displayed image is a 340 × 491 px detail cropped to Waxman.
media.title: Franz Waxman — Musical Courier, July 1955 (detail)

works.title: Trouble for Two
works.publicNote: Bronisław Kaper’s involvement is documented as probable background or uncredited cue work rather than a conventional on-screen score credit. Some of this material is associated with Franz Waxman.

contributions.scopeNote: Composer of the film score (AFI). The Jurmann estate cue list additionally records several cues written “in Zusammenarbeit mit Bronislaw Kaper, Franz Waxman”.
AFI credits Waxman as music director on this film, not as composer; Kaper and Jurmann are credited for music.
Composer of the complete film score; separately registered with Kaper and Jurmann as a co-author of the song “At night”.
Registered with Kaper and Jurmann as a co-author of this song; Waxman was also the credited composer of the film score.
